title: Sequencing deferral
body:
- pattern: Sequencing deferral — a drift-detector flags a gap (a tool not yet installed, a capability not yet hardened, a dependent not yet wired, a span not yet emitted, a test tier not yet built) whose resolution is a LATER, still-pending chunk's defined job. NOT Foundation-only: it equally covers a primitive shipping before its driver, a config landing before the runtime that traces it, and a gate deferred at /implement that the wrap light gate then runs green.
  verdict: routine
  note: builds land capabilities first and harden / depend on them in later chunks — expected ordering, NOT spec drift (the spec is right; the resolving chunk just hasn't run yet). Apply silently. Auditable caution — it is sequencing ONLY if a later chunk genuinely owns the resolution; a gap with NO resolving chunk anywhere in the route is real drift → escalate. And ownership is a ROUTE annotation (a CARRY/PREREQ pinned on the owning entry at route-resolve), never this note or prose — a note cannot verify delivery, and an owner-chunk can complete without delivering unless the obligation rides its line. A dismissal citing a route-sequenced owner whose entry is already `complete` is NOT routine — the owner came and went; escalate it.

title: Not this chunk's drift
body:
- pattern: Not this chunk's drift — the proposal names a symbol / dependency / section / surface that does NOT appear in the report's Changes as this chunk's work: a dependency the chunk never touched, a plan↔plan bind neither of whose sections it changed, an invariant already satisfied by shipped infrastructure it merely consumed, a pre-existing surface it only extended internally.
  verdict: routine
  note: reject — the report's Changes is the single source of what changed this wrap, so a detector firing on anything else has mis-fired (commonly by reading the doc's own history or rationale as a current gap). Verify against the report before dismissing. Caution: where the proposal is ACCURATE and the drift REAL but pre-existing across several artifacts the chunk did not touch, do NOT amend the one artifact the detector named — that leaves a worse spec-vs-impl mismatch; route the whole family to its OWNED channel instead: a `CARRY:` pin on the markerless entry that owns that surface (route-resolve, this wrap), or — when it belongs to a future version — an `.andromeda/residuals.md` append.

title: Registry over-reach
body:
- pattern: Registry over-reach — a detector proposes registering per-item REALIZATION into a spec registry that tracks its subject at CATEGORY grain: a public API symbol, an internal module, a CLI verb or flag, a command / handler name, an individual config file, a framework permission granted inside an already-registered capability file, a second transport instance for an already-registered surface.
  verdict: routine
  note: reject — the arch registries track occupied RESOURCES (ports / sockets / endpoints / IPC / events / env vars / crates/packages / artifacts) and contract SHAPES, not the realization inside an already-registered category. Check what the registry actually enumerates, and whether earlier chunks of the same kind registered theirs — they usually did not. A genuinely new resource of a kind the registry DOES enumerate still registers normally.

title: Accurate this-chunk addition
body:
- pattern: Accurate this-chunk addition — the proposal registers something the CURRENT chunk genuinely introduced or changed (its named symbols / values DO appear in the report's Changes), landing inside an existing section; or it reconciles a spec's illustrative wording / mechanism to the sound implementation the chunk shipped, where the report shows the invariant still holds.
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — the apply-side dual of the two reject rules above; without it a playbook only learns to dismiss. Bringing a body to current truth IS reconcile's job. The test is that the named thing is THIS chunk's and the invariant survives — only form or mechanism may differ. A REVERSAL of a locked decision is not this rule: escalate that once to ratify it.

title: External decay
body:
- pattern: External decay — a gate turns red with NO in-diff cause: the lock / source / config it checks is un-drifted and the failure keys on the world moving while the project stood still (a freshly-fetched advisory DB, an expired tool or cert, a registry policy change) — typically surfacing after a pause.
  verdict: routine
  note: neither this chunk's drift (nothing in the diff caused it) nor sequencing (no future chunk owns it yet) — the world moved, the code didn't. It never blocks the chunk that DISCOVERED it, and it never resolves by silently widening an ignore list (actionable-with-fix items are not the non-actionable class an ignore legitimately absorbs). It ALWAYS produces an owner: a route entry, or a recorded bounded deferral. If the gate must pass meanwhile, an ID-scoped reasoned ignore NAMING its owning chunk is part of the pattern, not a shortcut — a permanently-red gate stops discriminating, so a NEW red becomes invisible. An operator-RATIFIED standing deferral may compact its re-pin and set a probe re-run interval — with the overlap probe NAMED and verified green every chunk, and interval skips recorded in the chunk report, never silent — or take the probe-auto-satisfy tier: the pin names its SIGNATURE (failing gate's exit + first diagnostic line + overlap result) and a byte-identical probe — read from the external artifact's current state, never only a local copy of it — satisfies it with a one-line record; any deviation restores the full form.

title: Boundary widening
body:
- pattern: Boundary widening — a chunk WIDENS what crosses an already-hardened boundary (a read-only channel gains a write, a validated surface admits a new input class, a subprocess/IPC boundary gains a new crossing) and the proposal records it.
  verdict: escalate
  note: always a human's call — never mint a routine rule for this class, however often it recurs: the recurrence is the reason it must keep reaching the operator (a routine verdict here silently widens a precedent). The escalation resolves on the operator's ratification, recorded in the sidecar.

title: A field inside a ratified carrier
body:
- pattern: A field inside a ratified carrier — a chunk adds a new field of a closed value set (a fixed word, a boolean, a closed enum; never authored text) inside a carrier whose crossing is already ratified, with no new carrier, verb, argument, exit or log field, and the proposal records it.
  verdict: routine
  note: not a boundary widening and does not come to the founder — recorded as an inventory fact of the ratified crossing. Every qualifier is a precondition: a field holding authored or free text, an open value set, a new carrier or exit, or a carrier never ratified is the Boundary widening rule's and escalates. Set by the founder as the stated price of his answer to fork 1 of 2026-10-10-snapshot-states (word: «Внутри ратифицированного» — the founder, 2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer); appended at that chunk's wrap on his confirm of the rule in full with its preconditions (word: «Подтвердить всё» — the founder, 2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer, given as the operator's answer at the wrap's Validate card).

title: The program's own fixed text inside a ratified carrier
body:
- pattern: The program's own fixed text inside a ratified carrier — a chunk sends out, on a carrier whose crossing is already ratified, text the program itself holds as `'static` data of its one table (a verb's help, a remedy, the self-description, an error's fixed message), with no new carrier or exit, and the proposal records it.
  verdict: routine
  note: not a boundary widening and does not come to the founder — recorded as an inventory fact of the ratified crossing. Every qualifier is a precondition: text from a page, a call or a screen, text built at run time from anything but the table, a new carrier or a new exit is the Boundary widening rule's and escalates. Set by the founder's answer to fork 1 of 2026-10-12-self-description (word: «Внутри, с правилом» — the founder, 2026-10-12, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer, inputs#I3); appended at that chunk's wrap on the operator's confirm.

title: Provisional discharge
body:
- pattern: Provisional discharge — an amendment removes, or would leave standing past its epoch, a PROVISIONAL mark: a body, key-file or sidecar clause recorded on a relayed rendering or a delegate's answer to a call the founder owns (a boundary widening, a trajectory call, a behaviour change for every document).
  verdict: escalate
  note: PROVISIONAL items are discharged in one batch at each epoch boundary, on the founder's own word — given at that wrap or relayed verbatim — never one at a time as chunks pass and never by a wrap on its own judgement. The wrap that closes an epoch (or the first wrap after it) lists every standing mark with its sites — bodies, key files, sidecars and leaves — for the operator; each one the founder rules on is ratified in the same pass (the mark replaced by `ratified by the founder ({date})`, the ratification recorded in the sidecar, any part still owed — a witness, a measurement — kept in the body beside it) or reworked; one with no ruling stays marked and is named in the handoff. Set by the founder at the Epoch 2 boundary (2026-10-06, `architecture-amendments.md`, the founder-rulings entry); written here on the operator's direction, 2026-10-07.

title: A proposal graded `escalate` by a detector's own severity, where that detector reports its invariant holding and the pla
body:
- pattern: A proposal graded `escalate` by a detector's own severity, where that detector reports its invariant holding and the plan's reviewed list names the change, is applied without a halt.
  verdict: routine
  note: the grade is the detector's severity for a VIOLATION of its invariant; a return that reports the invariant holding and proposes only the doc's stale wording has found none, and the change was already in front of the operator in the plan's reviewed `Expected amendments (wrap)` list. A `dependent-of` proposal — another wording of the claim the named change retires — is validated with its primary. It never covers a boundary widening, which is judged by its subject and escalates whatever a plan or a direction says, and it never discharges a PROVISIONAL mark. The class reached four wraps, all on 2026-10-07 (the 06-51 wrap escalated it; the 08-23, 12-34 and 14-22 wraps applied it). Appended on the founder's word (2026-10-07, relayed verbatim by the overseer); the pattern is the sentence the 2026-10-07T12-34-00 wrap proposed it in.

title: A spec claim a chunk's measurement disproves, about code the chunk did not edit, is amended to the measured limit and it
body:
- pattern: A spec claim a chunk's measurement disproves, about code the chunk did not edit, is amended to the measured limit and its fix pinned as a CARRY; routine.
  verdict: routine
  note: both halves are the rule — the body states the measured limit, and the fix is owned by a `CARRY:` on a route entry. Appended on the founder's ruling (word: "Добавить" — the founder, 2026-10-09, given by question dialog in the overseer session and relayed verbatim by the overseer); the pattern is the overseer's rendering of the option he chose, in the directive for the 2026-10-09T19-17-00 0-pending wrap (`relay-1.md` in that run dir, item 3). That wrap could not write it — the 0-pending path's one playbook door is the seed-rule supersession — and carried it in the handoff to the 2026-10-09-audit-corrections-agent-surfaces wrap, which appended it on the operator's resume line.

title: Boundary widening by upstream merge
body:
- pattern: Boundary widening by upstream merge — a boundary widening that arrives with an upstream merge (upstream changed what crosses an already-hardened boundary, and the sync brought it in with no code of ours) and the proposal records it.
  verdict: escalate
  note: a facet of the Boundary widening rule above — a widening that arrives by an upstream merge is recorded PROVISIONAL for the founder like any other: the founder's own word decides it also when the change is upstream's. The record states what widened, whether a test of ours or of the merged delta covers it, and whether escher routes agent- or user-supplied input through the path today; the mark is discharged by the Provisional discharge rule. Appended on the founder's word (word: "Добавить" — the founder, 2026-10-10, given by question dialog in the overseer session and relayed by the overseer); proposed at the 2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces wrap from the operator's note at its escalation, and appended by the 2026-10-10-driver-cli wrap on the operator's resume line.

title: An engine behaviour change for every document
body:
- pattern: An engine behaviour change for every document — a chunk changes what the inherited engine does for every document, not only escher's — on the founder's own word at that chunk's P4 fork (given by him or relayed verbatim), and the proposal records it.
  verdict: routine
  note: the founder's answer to the fork is the ratification, recorded 'ratified by the founder ({date})' with his word, its merge surface owned by a CARRY on the upstream-sync entry. A delegate's answer or a relay not verbatim is PROVISIONAL (Provisional discharge rule); a change with no fork answer, or one that widens what crosses a boundary, escalates. Appended at the 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot wrap (fork 2, «Движок маскирует»).

title: A master's spelling of the founder's word follows its amendment's
body:
- pattern: A master's spelling of the founder's word follows its amendment's — where a sidecar entry's **Why:** is respelled to the verbatim form, every master line that copies that entry takes the same form, naming the labels the entry names; a line that copies another entry, or a genuine overseer relay, keeps its spelling.
  verdict: routine
  note: provenance only — the respelling moves no claim, ratification or PROVISIONAL mark, and each changed and each left site is listed with the entry it follows or its one reason. Appended on the founder's word (word: «Добавить правило (Рекомендую)» — the founder, 2026-10-13, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label; the English wording is the overseer's, inputs#I5), proposed at the 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship wrap's answer card after the overseer's directive (inputs#I4 item 2) settled its first case.

title: D-arch-resources
body:
- id: D-arch-resources
  doc: arch
  invariant: every new IPC method / endpoint / event / socket / port / env var / workspace crate/package the chunk lands is registered in arch §Occupied Resources / §Standard Contracts / §Inherited Defaults workspace crates/packages.
  check: agent-read — for each new symbol / API / crate/package in the report's Changes, confirm it appears in the arch registry sections; an unregistered resource is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-arch-decisions
body:
- id: D-arch-decisions
  doc: arch
  invariant: the chunk uses only the stack / runtime / patterns arch §Stack + §Established Decisions allow.
  check: agent-read — compare the report's Dependencies + symbols against §Stack / §Established Decisions; a new library, runtime, or a contradicted locked decision is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-security-input
body:
- id: D-security-input
  doc: security-plan
  invariant: every new external-input surface (IPC / HTTP / deserialized struct) the chunk adds is validated per §Input Validation.
  check: agent-read — for each new external-input symbol in the report, confirm the validation mechanism §Input Validation mandates is present; an unvalidated boundary is drift.
  severity: escalate

title: D-security-auth
body:
- id: D-security-auth
  doc: security-plan
  invariant: the auth / crypto / secret handling the chunk uses matches §Authentication + §Secret Management (no off-spec auth library or secret source).
  check: agent-read — if the report touches identity / session / token / keys, confirm the library + flow match §Authentication / §Secret Management; a mismatch is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-security-deps
body:
- id: D-security-deps
  doc: security-plan
  invariant: every new dependency the chunk adds is allowed by §Dependency Security (not on the ban list).
  check: agent-read — check the report's new Dependencies against the §Dependency Security bans; a banned / unvetted dependency is drift.
  severity: escalate

title: D-design-tokens
body:
- id: D-design-tokens
  doc: design-system
  invariant: new UI the chunk renders uses design tokens, not hardcoded values.
  check: agent-read — read the Coverage `tokens` flag of each new UI element in the report; `hardcoded✗` is drift against §Color Palette / §Spacing / §Typography.
  severity: warning

title: D-layout-surface
body:
- id: D-layout-surface
  doc: layout-templates
  invariant: a new user-facing surface / region the chunk adds is described in §Primary Surfaces / the wireframes.
  check: agent-read — if the report adds a UI surface or region, confirm it maps to a §Wireframe entry; an undocumented surface is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-tests-coverage
body:
- id: D-tests-coverage
  doc: test-plan
  invariant: new code paths the chunk adds carry tests at the tier the test-plan requires (§2 Test Strategy).
  check: agent-read — compare the report's new symbols / modules against its Outcome (tests run); a new path with no test at the mandated tier is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-tests-framework
body:
- id: D-tests-framework
  doc: test-plan
  invariant: the test framework / runner the chunk uses matches the test-plan (§2 + §4 unit strategy).
  check: agent-read — compare the report's test commands / runner against §2 / §4; an off-spec framework or runner is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-tests-obs-harness
body:
- id: D-tests-obs-harness
  doc: test-plan
  invariant: the 5-command harness / status shape / log format stays consistent between test-plan §3 and obs-plan §3.
  check: agent-read — if the report changes the harness, status endpoint, or log format, confirm §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree; a one-sided change is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-obs-instrumentation
body:
- id: D-obs-instrumentation
  doc: obs-plan
  invariant: new hot-path operations the chunk adds carry the spans / metrics / logs §4–§6 require.
  check: agent-read — for each new operation symbol in the report, confirm instrumentation per §4 / §5 / §6; an uninstrumented hot path is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-obs-stack
body:
- id: D-obs-stack
  doc: obs-plan
  invariant: the logging / telemetry library the chunk uses matches the obs harness §3.
  check: agent-read — compare the report's telemetry Dependencies / symbols against §3; an off-spec logger or OTel setup is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-obs-pii
body:
- id: D-obs-pii
  doc: obs-plan
  invariant: the chunk does not log raw user input / PII (§8 PII Scrubbing).
  check: agent-read — if the report adds logging that touches user data, confirm redaction per §8; raw PII in logs is drift.
  severity: escalate

title: D-a11y-surface
body:
- id: D-a11y-surface
  doc: a11y-plan
  invariant: a new interactive UI element the chunk adds carries the WCAG / focus / keyboard coverage §5–§7 require.
  check: agent-read — if the report adds an interactive UI element, confirm a11y coverage per §5 / §6 / §7; an uncovered element is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-a11y-obs-schema
body:
- id: D-a11y-obs-schema
  doc: a11y-plan
  invariant: the a11y violation JSON schema stays consistent with obs §6 (the structured-log schema a11y emits to).
  check: agent-read — if the report changes the a11y violation schema or the obs log schema, confirm the two still match; a divergence is drift.
  severity: warning

title: 2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits

Today's rule: the author key, else a component path whose segments read `{tag}[{key}]` for a Dioxus-keyed root and `{tag}:{n}` otherwise, `n` the index among same-owner, same-tag element siblings (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge); hypothesis: an edit that adds or removes an earlier same-tag sibling, or wraps an element, changes an unkeyed element's id (not measured). Which edits must keep the id is settled at this entry's promotion

title: 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema
body: CARRY: time and loads over the wire (from 2026-10-07-settle-detection) — settle is built in process only (`Harness::settle`, `Session::act`): it advances no time and waits on no load — time on a held instance moves only when its caller delivers ticks, and a load in flight is reported at once as `NotSettled(Loads)`. Two questions for this entry's verbs: how an agent moves the Timer's time through a driver session (the session host holds the tick handle and delivers nothing, examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:34-45), and whether a driver command may wait on a load with a clock — a new decision for security-plan §API Security, not an extension of settle. v010-10's driver leg, carried on "Act by id", cannot be proven until the first is answered

title: 2026-10-07-act-by-id
body: CARRY: v010-03's driver leg (from 2026-10-06-snapshot-model) — id coherence (v010-03) is unclaimed and named on no markerless entry: its accessibility-tree leg and its snapshot leg are built and proven (`stand_accessibility_ids`, `stand_snapshot`: the snapshot's ids equal the tree's `author_id`s and each element's `element_id`), and the remaining leg is the driver's — the id an action takes is that same id; this entry is where the three-way check can first pass  CARRY: input the engine cannot take headlessly (from 2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity; the direction given at that chunk's P5 review that each engine defect it found gets a route owner, and the operator's fifth item given at its operator pass, 2026-10-06 — the wrap's placement) — (1) on macOS the editor has no Backspace arm (text.rs:330-331 leaves the delete to the Apple standard key bindings), so a headless key press deletes nothing there (measured: CI#37539756517, `Test (macos)`); the driver needs typed deletion that works headless on every platform; (2) the engine has no `select` or range interaction model, so the stand's `timer-duration` slider reads its value yet cannot be changed through input; hypothesis for (2): read from the code at that chunk's phase (construct.rs:440-459 gives special data only to text-entry inputs, textareas, checkboxes and radios), not measured by driving a range input  CARRY: v010-06's driver leg (from 2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff; the operator's direction at that chunk's P5 review, 2026-10-07) — v010-06 is unclaimed: its in-process legs are built and proven — the truthful change flag and its drain (`BaseDocument::has_changes` / `take_changed_nodes`; the `changed_set_` unit tests) and the diff (`Snapshot::diff(&self, after: &Snapshot) -> SnapshotDiff`; `stand_diff`: exact per step against the check's own oracle, empty for a step that changes nothing, equal in both layout modes); this entry's act returns that diff unchanged and claims v010-06; the engine's changed set is not the diff — it is engine-touched, and the flag true beside an empty diff is a designed case (architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Invalidation and state integrity); a diff carries ids, accessible names and a text control's value and leaves the process through the returned value only (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07; security-plan §Input Validation, the `id` row) — the first command that returns it asks the crossing question again  CARRY: typed text in a sink-installing host's log (from 2026-10-07-driver-session; the founder's ruling, 2026-10-07, relayed verbatim — the sink fix is proven with a typed sentinel once a command can type) — when this entry gives the driver a command that types into a held instance, prove a typed sentinel occurs 0 times in the `escher-session` binary's stderr at `RUST_LOG=trace`; typed text is unmeasured today, no command being able to type into the binary's instance (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-session/evidence/host-stderr-by-level.md); if another entry delivers a typing command first, the proof is that entry's; since 2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist the sink drops every outside-target record and the standing check to extend is seven_guis' `host_log`, which already reads that binary's stderr at `trace` with needles read from the stand (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist/report.md)  CARRY: the session library's accessibility feature (from 2026-10-07-driver-session) — `escher-driver` names no `dioxus-native-dom` feature, so nothing reads a snapshot or a diff through the library today; the entry that first reads the snapshot through a session decides the feature, and naming it in `escher-driver` reaches the windowed stand binary's own build through `seven_guis → escher-driver` (a11y-plan §1 A11y Scope Summary, Dioxus crates; architecture §Established Decisions → [Driver session])  CARRY: v010-10's driver leg (from 2026-10-07-settle-detection; the operator, 2026-10-07, at that chunk's P5 review) — settle (v010-10) is unclaimed and named on no other markerless entry: its in-process leg is built and proven (`Harness::settle`, `Session::act`, `stand_settle`), and the remaining leg is the driver's — a driver action on the Timer returning settled with the delayed update present. Measured at that chunk (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-settle-detection/evidence/red-first.md): a step that clicks Reset and then delivers three ticks reads `0.0s` with no pass after the delivery and `0.3s` once settled, so the Timer check is red without the settle — the plan had predicted it green, one of the three reasons given for not claiming the cap there; the other two stand (an in-process closure is no action an agent can run; under `escher-session` nobody delivers the ticks). The time question carried on "Command and refusal schema" is answered (2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema; the operator, 2026-10-07, at that chunk's P4 forks): time moves by the `advance` verb, in milliseconds, through a step the session's caller supplies — stated in the schema, wired nowhere; the leg now waits on that wiring, the next annotation  CARRY: the wiring of `advance` (from 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema; the operator, 2026-10-07, at that chunk's P4 forks) — the schema states the verb (`advance`, `ms` 1 to 60000, result `advanced_ms`, the cause `time-unavailable`) and nothing moves time through a session: `validate` only checks the call. Owed here: the step a session's caller supplies at start; the stand host's mapping of milliseconds onto Timer ticks (one tick is 0.1 s, examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:57-60), what it does with a remainder and reports as `advanced_ms`, never more than asked; whether the harness's own clock moves with it (`Harness::tick`, packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:152-155); and `time-unavailable` for a session with no step. The host cannot reach the tick handle while it serves — `serve` consumes the session and blocks in accept (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:48) — so the step is handed to the session, not held by the binary (coordinates as read at that chunk's research; the three files are unchanged since). The acting verbs' shapes are the schema's: `click` and `type` take an `id`, `press` a `key` and an optional `shift`, and each returns `settled` · `busy` · `added` · `removed` · `changed` — a step that ran and did not go quiet is a result, not a refusal

title: 2026-10-07-refusal-detection
body: CARRY: minimal fixture for the covered case (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-06, given as the 2026-10-06-snapshot-model wrap's directive) — the stand is the proof, plus minimal fixtures beside it for cases the 7GUIs tasks lack; an element covered by another is the named one, so this cause is proven on such a fixture (intent §Principles, "The stand is the proof"; v010-11's acceptance still reads "On the stand" — see its ledger note)  CARRY: the causes are named and worded, not detected (from 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema) — `escher_driver::Cause` holds the five screen-level causes (`not-found` · `stale` · `disabled` · `covered` · `off-screen`) with fixed meanings and remedies, and `validate` returns `unknown-verb` and `malformed` only; since 2026-10-07-act-by-id the executor returns `not-found` — for an id no element of the screen reads, the id of a row the driver just deleted included (measured at tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_refused.rs) — and nothing returns the other four yet. Two decisions for this entry: telling `stale` from `not-found` needs the session to remember the ids it has read (it holds a label, the harness and an optional time step, and looks an id up anew on every call); and the `off-screen` remedy reads "bring it into view" while the verb table has no verb that scrolls — a verb joining the table, or an action that brings its target into view itself. `disabled` is stated on the snapshot's presence reading (`enabled`), never the attribute's value; a cause's texts are reworded only with a recorded reason  CARRY: what a click does to a target that cannot take it (from 2026-10-07-act-by-id) — the executor detects none of `disabled`, `covered` and `off-screen`: a driver click on such a target runs, returns settled, and its diff says what changed — on the stand a click on the disabled `crud-delete` returns an empty diff (measured at tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_ids.rs); this entry's detection goes in front of that click, in `escher_driver`'s executor (packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs), and a refusal must leave the instance unchanged, as `stand_act_refused` proves today for `unknown-verb`, `malformed` and `not-found`

title: 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans
body: CARRY: the sink's target allowlist (from 2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist) — a span or event reaches a sink-installing binary's stderr only under an engine target or a target starting `escher_`; one logged under any other target, the stand's own `seven_guis` path included, is dropped whole at every level, so a span that is emitted and never printed is this rule, not a missing call site (measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist/evidence/by-level.md; obs-plan §8 → Scrubbing)  CARRY: the cause field's domain, and two fields never to add (from 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema) — the span's refusal-cause field takes an `escher_driver::Cause` name, one of eight fixed class words. No argument is fielded by its schema name, and no `Command`, `Call` or `ArgValue` with `Debug`: both print an id and typed text, and of the argument names only `text` is in the sink's scrub set — `id`, `key`, `shift` and `ms` are not (obs-plan §4; §8 → Scrubbing)  CARRY: the executor is the span's subject (from 2026-10-07-act-by-id) — `escher_driver::Session::run` runs every driver command in process and is silent by its chunk's constraint: the one span per command covers it — its settle wait (one `Harness::settle` per acting verb), its diff size (`Outcome`'s `SnapshotDiff`: added · removed · changed) and its refusal cause; `Outcome` joins `Command`, `Call` and `ArgValue` as a type never fielded with `Debug` — it prints ids, accessible names and control values; all eight cause names are returned since 2026-10-07-refusal-detection (`unknown-verb` and `malformed` by `validate`, the other six by the executor), and a sixth verb, `scroll`, returns `Outcome::Scrolled` — the same diff and a flag, `in_view`; a `scroll` of a nested box names that box among its changed nodes, so its diff size reads one node high (the CARRY on "Driver CLI", a scrolled box's own bounds)

title: 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep
body: CARRY: fixtures beside the stand (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-06, given as the 2026-10-06-snapshot-model wrap's directive) — everything built is validated: where the 7GUIs tasks lack a case, a minimal fixture beside the stand proves it, and the sweep counts those fixtures with the tasks (intent §Principles, "The stand is the proof")  CARRY: keys for the three non-lean tasks (from 2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits; whether a snapshot then says that an element reacts to a click, or the reading rides to a later version, is asked of the founder with that measurement  CARRY: what a hit still reaches, and what was not measured (from 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit, where the operator's answer of 2026-10-10 at the plan's forks set the stop at paint's overflow half; said by `covered`'s own meaning); not measured: a hit at an image's, a sub-document's and a text input's own box; no stand file sets `contain` (0 hits for the property in `examples/seven_guis`, read at that wrap), so the case is a fixture's; whether it is read, and as `checked` or as `pressed`, is decided at this entry's promotion  CARRY: whether Cells states its selected cell (from 2026-10-10-snapshot-states; leaned at that chunk's plan forks and confirmed by the operator at its plan review, 2026-10-10: untouched there, the question owed a route owner; placed here by the operator's direction at that chunk's wrap) — the flight booker and the CRUD state selected, pressed and invalid by attribute and a snapshot reads them; Cells was not edited, no headless check reads it, and it reads 676 unkeyed actionable elements (the keys CARRY above); the Linux figure is checked at the bound and one byte over (`cli_commands`: 94 holds a session, 95 ends `state-dir-too-long`, status `3`), the 90 is read from the code and not measured on any leg — a check at 90 and 91 on the macOS leg is owed  CARRY: a shot within 0.7 s of a scroll can differ (from 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot; no check measures it (the focused-caret check clicks past the text's end); hypothesis: a click-placed caret can say something of the value's glyph widths; measure it on a fixture beside the stand — a fix in the pointer path is an engine change for every document, a founder fork  CARRY: Circle Drawer's dialog rule (from 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship; placed here by that chunk's report) — upstream #1186 builds Dioxus attribute names in the empty namespace, so CSS attribute selectors now match Dioxus elements; `.cd-dialog input[type="range"]` (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs:215) is predicted to apply for the first time — hypothesis: unmeasured, the four lean tasks read no moved number  CARRY: two range paths that chunk edited hold no check (from 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction; Enter on a focused button that is itself scrolled reaches it as its own click (measured at 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, `stand_keyboard::a_button_that_is_itself_scrolled_takes_enter_as_its_own_click`);
